extracted.intended_audience: researchers and potential crowd reviewers interested in participating in ASAPbio's preprint crowd review (life sciences preprint community)
extracted.subtask_description: A coordinated crowd-review model for life-science preprints in which self-nominated researchers provide feedback via a collaborative document over a 14-day commenting period and produce a collective synthesis that is posted publicly on PREreview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with FAST principles for preprint feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members are asked to provide contributions in alignment with the FAST principles for preprint feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAST principles are referenced as the normative behavioral/quality framework for contributions; page links to more information about the crowd preprint review workflow but does not list the FAST principles on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review requested by
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the reviews are initiated by individuals or groups who are not the preprint authors (i.e., crowd-organized rather than author-requested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the crowd self-nominate to participate rather than being invited or assigned by an editor; organizers select which self-nominated reviewers are included per instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process does not incorporate open public commenting as an integral part of the review workflow (comments take place in a managed collaborative document and synthesized output is posted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of author response
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author responses are not incorporated into the crowd review process as an integral part; authors may optionally respond via PREreview or the preprint server but this is outside the core workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The crowd review service does not render editorial decisions or binary accept/reject recommendations; it provides synthesized feedback only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage (PReF)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PReF indicates that the group's evaluation activities are intended to cover the full manuscript, even though individual crowd members may focus on parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scope by interest/expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members can comment on the full paper or on parts of it, according to their interest and/or expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is flexible: reviewers may target sections where they have domain knowledge rather than being required to assess every element of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity known to editor/service
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity known to: Editor or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer identities are not publicly disclosed by default; they are recorded and visible to the organizing editors or service administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests not collected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crowd members are not asked to declare competing interests as part of the process described on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for pseudonymous contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members can use a pseudonym so that their identity is known only to organizers of the review activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workflow explicitly allows pseudonymous participation to protect reviewer privacy while still enabling organizers to track contributions; this is coupled with the lack of competing-interest declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No binary or scalar rating or recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The service provides no binary or scalar rating or recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback is qualitative and synthesized rather than summarized with scores or accept/reject recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow: selection, circulation, 14-day commenting period
rubrics_metrics.description: The ASAPbio crowds will select preprints to review and circulate them to crowd members for comments during the following 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process timeline: weekly selection and a defined two-week window for comment collection; organizers coordinate selection and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback format: collaborative Google document
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members will receive a weekly preprint and be invited to provide feedback on the paper via a collaborative Google document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary medium for collective commenting is a shared Google Doc, enabling synchronous/asynchronous collaborative annotation and discussion among crowd members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and publication of review
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the commenting period, a crowd member will generate a collective synthesis of the comments for each paper. The synthesized review will then be posted publicly on PREreview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One participant is responsible for producing a synthesized summary of crowd feedback which is then made publicly available on PREreview; the synthesis represents the group's view rather than an editorial decision and does not integrate author replies as part of the core output.
